A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SWITCH-A-VIEW and retain the same central approach and experiments. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and supplementary sections support comparison despite the changed title and expanded appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original view-switch detection and view-selection experiments on HowTo100M and Ego-Exo4D, including baseline comparisons, ablations and supplementary sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports new baseline comparisons, annotation-agreement statistics, stricter-consensus evaluations and joint-finetuning results.

M1.justification: v2 adds an evaluated optional joint-finetuning variant combining best-view supervision with a narration-derived pseudo-label loss (Section 7.4). The central detector-to-selector pipeline remains. Relative-time embeddings for frames also become explicit in Section 3.3, although the PDFs do not establish whether this is an implementation change or fuller documentation.

E1.justification: Both retain HowTo100M, Ego-Exo4D and Charades-Ego with the same central tasks. However, v1 describes five Ego-Exo4D test activity categories, whereas v2 lists six, despite retaining 2.7 hours and 5,049 test instances. The PDFs do not resolve whether coverage changed or the category description was corrected.

E2.justification: v2 adds InternVideo2 retrieval and view-narration similarity, a first-person-pronoun heuristic, and LangView-smallData/bigData comparisons (Tables 1–2). Earlier CLIP retrieval results remain in Tables 8–9; the unchanged CLIP-ViewSelect score row is now described as X-CLIP-based similarity. Sample-count and scenario plots replace CLIP-ViewSelect with LangView-bigData, substantially strengthening the comparator suite.

E3.justification: New evaluations use stricter consensus subsets requiring eight or nine agreeing annotators and compare LangView under two pretraining-data budgets. The main splits, metrics, teacher forcing and 5,000-label setting remain. v1's greater-than-70% rule and v2's stated seven-of-nine rule are effectively equivalent. Section 7.3 inconsistently labels some stricter percentages, but specifies the intended vote counts.

E4.justification: v2 adds sensitivity tests for annotation-consensus filtering (Table 5), a joint-supervision ablation (Figure 3b), and analysis across feature-encoder choices (Section 7.8). These examine label reliability and complementary supervision beyond v1's analyses. Existing input, shot-labeling and context-duration ablations remain; the scenario analysis is relocated and updated with a different comparator.

E5.justification: Beyond v1's agreement cutoff, v2 reports chance-corrected annotation agreement: Cohen's kappa of 0.65 for HowTo100M and 0.70 for Ego-Exo4D (Section 4). The existing p ≤ 0.05 reporting practice continues. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, seeds or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: The result set substantially expands with new comparators, stricter-consensus results and joint finetuning. For example, v2 reports 54.3/57.9/56.5 accuracy/AUC/AP for joint finetuning (Figure 3b), versus the standard model's unchanged 54.0/57.3/56.0 in both versions. LangView-bigData newly scores 54.5 AP against 56.0 for SWITCH-A-VIEW. These are added experimental comparisons, not improved scores for the unchanged original configuration.

T1.justification: v2 introduces a distinct mathematical objective for joint finetuning: best-view cross-entropy plus a weighted narration-pseudo-label cross-entropy term (Equation 8). Most other added equations formalize operations already described in v1, and the original losses are retained with new numbering. Neither version develops theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claim of learning view selection from unlabeled, edited videos remains. v2 additionally makes headline claims about substantial human agreement on the best view and superiority over state-of-the-art view selection and multimodal retrieval. The abstract no longer presents introducing a few-shot setting as a separate contribution.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the agreement statistics as evidence that subjective best-view choices can be evaluated reliably, and joint finetuning as showing complementarity with LangView's supervision. It also attributes InternVideo2's advantages over CLIP-style baselines to finer features and temporal context. Existing failure conditions are largely retained in shorter form.

D1.justification: v2 documents temporal discretization into 0.1-second bins, binary view-embedding lookup keys, ten-instance annotator qualifiers with a 90% passing requirement, and validation-based selection of the joint-loss weight 0.3. These add reproducibility information without establishing that previously reported experiments were rerun. Most architecture, optimizer and training details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: LangView was already cited in v1, but v2 treats it explicitly as a state-of-the-art comparator and a complementary supervision approach, replacing the baseline discussion's no-prior-work premise. InternVideo2, X-CLIP and agreement-statistics references are added. The broader related-work categories and positioning around learning from unlabeled instructional videos remain.

P1.justification: Substantial editing spans the title, abstract, task explanation, model exposition and results narrative. 'Few-shot' is systematically reframed as 'limited labels', and next-view prediction is explained more explicitly. Section 4 is reorganized around datasets and annotations, while scenario analysis moves into a restructured and expanded supplement.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redesigned and moved before the abstract. Figure 3 becomes a two-panel display, the scenario chart is relocated and replotted, and comparison tables are expanded with earlier CLIP results redisplayed in the appendix. Annotation-interface figures replace empty video and text placeholders with visible examples. The architecture diagram remains largely unchanged.

improvement.justification: v1's empirical case relied on heuristics and CLIP-style comparisons and documented annotation reliability mainly through a cutoff. v2 adds a trained task-specific competitor under two data budgets, stronger representation baselines, and consensus-sensitivity tests (Tables 1–2 and 5). These address important weaknesses in comparative and ground-truth validation, substantially strengthening support for the central contribution despite unchanged original scores. Category-count ambiguity and inconsistent threshold wording limit reporting precision but do not outweigh these gains.
